output.brief: The gap is mostly not about where people work. Remote staff are less often eligible for promotion: only 32% of them have 18+ months in level, against 74% of office staff. Among eligible employees, remote and office rates are nearly the same (20.0% vs 21.1% approved), and nomination rates match (28.2% vs 28.6%). The dashboard compares everyone, so it mixes in tenure. The proximity-bias explanation is not supported, so the three-office-day rule should not be announced; it would penalise remote staff, including about 180 who live far from an office and were hired on home-based contracts. Next: have People Analytics re-run the comparison among eligible staff, and look at how remote people are getting time-in-level and access to stretch work. Stretch work cannot currently be measured, so that question is open. Confidence is moderate: the eligible-group gap rests on 110 remote staff and could be a few points either way. Attrition has not been checked.
